name: Vemurafenib
route_note: oral tablets 960 mg twice daily, alone or with cobimetinib

discovery.by: Plexxikon (Gideon Bollag, Kam Zhang and colleagues)
discovery.note: Discovered by fragment-based, structure-guided design starting from a 7-azaindole scaffold.

tagline: First BRAF V600E inhibitor, a fragment-based design for metastatic melanoma
summary: Vemurafenib is a selective inhibitor of BRAF kinase carrying the V600E mutation, found in about half of melanomas. It produced rapid tumour shrinkage and improved survival in BRAF-mutant metastatic melanoma and is also approved for Erdheim–Chester disease; it is now mostly used with the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib.
mechanism: BRAF V600E is a constitutively active kinase that signals as a monomer through MEK and ERK to drive proliferation. Vemurafenib binds the active conformation of mutant BRAF and blocks MAPK pathway signalling.

In cells with wild-type BRAF and active RAS, the drug paradoxically promotes RAF dimerisation and activates ERK, which explains new keratoacanthomas and squamous cell carcinomas; adding a MEK inhibitor reduces this effect and delays resistance.
uses: Unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation (alone or with cobimetinib)
Erdheim–Chester disease with BRAF V600 mutation

history.title: BRAF mutations
history.detail: Davies et al. (Nature, Sanger Institute) find activating BRAF mutations in about 66% of melanomas, mostly V600E.

history.title: Phase I results
history.detail: Flaherty et al. (NEJM) report high response rates in BRAF V600E melanoma.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: BRIM-3 shows a survival benefit over dacarbazine; approved with the cobas 4800 BRAF test.

history.title: Erdheim–Chester disease
history.detail: FDA approves vemurafenib for BRAF V600-mutant Erdheim–Chester disease.

serious: cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and keratoacanthoma

facts: It was one of the first approved drugs discovered by fragment-based screening.
